Subjunctive in Relative Clauses (Known vs. Unknown Antecedent)
Signaling whether the referent exists/is known or is hypothetical
Antecedent + que + Indicative (specific/known) | Subjunctive (non-specific/nonexistent)
Busco a un traductor que domina el japonés.
BOOS-koh ah oon trah-dook-TOHR keh doh-MEE-nah ehl hah-poh-NEHS
I am looking for a (specific) translator who masters Japanese.
Busco un traductor que domine tres idiomas.
BOOS-koh oon trah-dook-TOHR keh doh-MEE-neh trehs ee-DYOH-mahs
I am looking for any translator who masters three languages.
Future & Conditional of Probability
Expressing conjecture about the present or past without 'tal vez'
Future tense (present conjecture) | Conditional tense (past conjecture)
¿Dónde estará Elena? Estará en la biblioteca.
DOHN-deh ehs-tah-RAH eh-LEH-nah? ehs-tah-RAH ehn lah bee-blyoh-TEH-kah
Where could Elena be? She's probably in the library.
Serían las diez cuando terminó el debate.
seh-REE-ahn lahs dyehs KWAHN-doh tehr-mee-NOH ehl deh-BAH-teh
It must have been around ten when the debate ended.
Verbs of Becoming (hacerse / volverse / llegar a ser / quedarse)
Choosing the exact verb for transformation or change of state
hacerse (voluntary/gradual) | volverse (sudden/involuntary) | llegar a ser (culmination) | quedarse (resulting state)
Con esfuerzo, llegó a ser directora del instituto.
kohn ehs-FWEHR-soh yeh-GOH ah sehr dee-rehk-TOH-rah dehl eens-tee-TOO-toh
With effort, she eventually became director of the institute.
Se quedó sorprendido al oír la noticia.
seh keh-DOH sohr-prehn-DEE-doh ahl oh-EER lah noh-TEE-syah
He was left surprised upon hearing the news.
